decisions.quote: Overall, we found empirical support for the hypothesis that gratitude and indebtedness are correlated to expectation for reciprocity, yet failed to find support for the association between expectation for reciprocity and reciprocity inclination.Our findings support the argument by Watkins et al. [6] that expectation for reciprocity would be associated with higher indebtedness but lower gratitude. Provided that benevolent helping intent is associated with lower expectations for reciprocity, then according to the experimental paradigm of Watkins et al. [6], it would be associated with decreased indebtedness and increased gratitude. Our extensions help link between Tsang [1] and Watkins et al. [6] into a more comprehensive theory that higher benevolent intent is correlated with lower expectations and therefore higher gratitude than indebtedness.
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files were checked and are absent for this never-adjudicated work. Although framed under the paper's 'Extensions' to Study 3 (n = 759 US Prolific participants), the authors explicitly formulate pre-registered Hypotheses 13, 14, and 15 to empirically retest the published findings of Watkins et al. (2006) [6] described in Sections 1.1.1 and 1.5—specifically that higher expectations of reciprocity are associated with decreased gratitude (H14) and increased indebtedness (H15), and that weaker expectations of reciprocity are associated with stronger willingness/inclination to reciprocate (H13). In Section 3.2, they test these hypotheses via Pearson correlations, finding support for H14 (gratitude and perceived reciprocity expectations: r(757) = -0.28, p < 0.001) and H15 (indebtedness and perceived reciprocity expectations: r(757) = 0.17, p < 0.001), but no support for H13 (reciprocity inclination and perceived reciprocity expectations: r(757) = -0.06, p = 0.08), and in Section 4.2 they explicitly compare their empirical results to Watkins et al. [6]. Per codebook rules, testing whether a specific published result holds in a new sample and comparing the results against that original qualifies as a replication target regardless of whether the section is labeled an extension. The sole shipped row (input_row_index 2243) is Tsang (2006) ('The Effects of Helper Intention on Gratitude and Indebtedness', Motivation and Emotion, DOI 10.1007/s11031-006-9031-z, sibling target_index 0). Watkins, Scheer, Ovnicek, and Kolts (2006) ('The debt of gratitude: dissociating gratitude and indebtedness', Cognition and Emotion, 20, 217-241, DOI 10.1080/02699930500172291) is a distinct original paper by different authors in a different journal and is also distinct from sibling targets 2 (Bartlett & DeSteno, 2006) and 3 (Peng et al., 2020).
